key_insight: BISECT counters spectral starvation in continual LoRA learning by splitting a fixed low-rank budget between shared invariant features and task-specific novelty.
engineering_relevance: For engineering vision workflows with sequentially arriving tasks, BISECT offers a potential adaptation strategy without added inference parameters or FLOPs, though solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated.
method: Extract invariant directions from dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix.
Build an orthogonal novelty block using generalized Rayleigh whitening and complement projection.
Fold trained updates into the frozen backbone, scaling invariant atoms by current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios and retaining novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that historical null tails capture only 5.5% of incoming-task variance and that BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight incremental settings on five vision datasets.
watch_item: Training-time costs and numerical stability of Gram-matrix estimation and generalized Rayleigh whitening are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
